comment: The one source of truth for what changed in each release. The app shows these in its What's New window; Scripts/release.sh turns the matching entry into the appcast description Sparkle shows before installing, and into the GitHub release body. Newest first. A release with no entry here is refused by release.sh. Add "showsWelcome": true to an entry to show updating users the welcome window itself instead of these notes — for a release that changes how Perch introduces itself. Their existing settings are pre-filled, so the window changes nothing they do not change.

versions.headline: The first launch now explains itself.

highlights.title: A welcome on first launch
highlights.detail: New installs get a short window explaining the two gestures Perch is built on, and Launch at Login is a checkbox you tick rather than a decision made for you.

highlights.title: Pick where the shelf lives
highlights.detail: Choose which screen edges it may use, then watch a shelf appear at every one of them at once. The notch is offered only on Macs that have one.

highlights.title: The shelf starts on the left
highlights.detail: New installs open on the left edge instead of the right.

highlights.title: ⌘-drag is discoverable
highlights.detail: The shelf could always be pulled off its edge to float anywhere, but nothing said so. Its menu now names the gesture, and stops once you have used it.
